commit_message:
[gxvar] Reduce number of mallocs.

8% speed up in drawing GoogleSansFlex variable in HB benchmark-font.

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas): Use an allocation
  pool instead of individual allocations.

8% speed up in drawing GoogleSansFlex variable in HB benchmark-font.

* src/truetype/ttgxvar.c (TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas): Use an allocation

findings.title: gvar pool undersized for peak_coords due to missing sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier
findings.message: In TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas(), the refactor to a single shared allocation pool computes peak_coords_size as ALIGN_SIZE(3 * blend->num_axis) — the number of FT_Fixed elements needed — but omits the `* sizeof (FT_Fixed)` factor that every other sub-buffer in the same pool_size computation includes (point_deltas_x_size, points_org_size, points_out_size, has_delta_size all multiply by the element size). Since peak_coords is declared as FT_Fixed* and is later indexed/written as `peak_coords[...]`, `im_start_coords = peak_coords + blend->num_axis`, etc. over 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values (12 bytes typically with sizeof(FT_Fixed)==4), the pool reserves only 3*num_axis BYTES instead of 3*num_axis*sizeof(FT_Fixed) bytes — a ~4x (sizeof(FT_Fixed)) undersizing of this sub-region. Because peak_coords sits at the start of the single pool buffer and all subsequent sub-buffers (point_deltas_x, points_org, points_out, has_delta) are laid out contiguously immediately after it via pointer arithmetic (`p += peak_coords_size`), writes to peak_coords/im_start_coords/im_end_coords beyond the tiny reserved region overflow into adjacent pool memory and, for fonts with enough axes/points, past the end of the heap allocation entirely, causing a heap buffer overflow (OOB write) when applying glyph variation deltas from a crafted variable font's `gvar` table.
findings.suggestion: Multiply peak_coords_size by sizeof(*peak_coords) (i.e. sizeof(FT_Fixed)) just like the other pool sub-buffer sizes, so the allocation reflects the true byte size needed for 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values.

ground_truth.root_cause: Inconsistent/incomplete arithmetic when converting an array-element-count-based allocation macro (FT_QNEW_ARRAY, which handles sizeof internally) into a manual pool-size computation; the sizeof multiplier for one of five sub-buffers (peak_coords, an FT_Fixed array) was dropped while it was correctly applied to the other four, so the pool undersizes the first field by a factor of sizeof(FT_Fixed).

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: gvar pool undersized for peak_coords due to missing sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier
